project_name: DII Common Operating Environment XML Services
initial_requirements: Defense mission and support applications need common XML services within the Defense Information Infrastructure operating environment. The services should let authorized users and applications register shared terms and structures, define reusable XML schemas, and create or consume XML documents. They should also provide vendor-independent access to distributed information so applications can exchange and manage data without depending on a particular physical database implementation.

topics.topic_content: Why common XML services are needed across defense mission and support applications

slots.key: Operational problem or interoperability gap
slots.value: Different applications often represent the same business data in different ways, which makes sharing and integration slow and brittle. Common XML services are meant to provide a shared, controlled way to define and exchange that data so applications can interoperate more reliably, reducing custom point-to-point translations, duplicate definitions, and the effort needed to keep systems talking to each other.

slots.key: Discovery and update access controls for registered definitions
slots.value: Discovery and reuse should be further limited when a definition is still in draft, has export or distribution restrictions, or is tied to a sensitive mission area where only a subset of users should even know it exists. Reuse may also be limited if a schema is marked for a particular program or enclave and has not been approved for broader use. If someone requests an update without approval, the system should not let them modify the registered version directly; it should either reject the change with a clear message or route it into a review workflow, depending on the governance process. For official exchange, reporting, and integration, users and systems should only be allowed to discover and use the authoritative version. Local or alternate versions can be available for internal drafting or staging only if the user has the right permissions, and they should be clearly labeled as non-authoritative so they can’t be mistaken for the approved standard. If the content is sensitive or controlled, discovery should be limited even further so only authorized roles can see that the alternate version exists at all. The service should enforce both access control and status-based rules so the wrong version cannot be selected for formal use by accident.

slots.key: Discovery and use rules for authoritative versus local XML versions
slots.value: For official exchange, reporting, and integration, only the authoritative version should be discoverable and usable. Local or alternate versions may be available for internal drafting, staging, draft, test, or internal contexts only when the user has permission to use non-authoritative content, and they must be clearly kept marked as local or variant so they are not promoted or treated as the approved standard by default. If the reuse is for an official managed process, only the authoritative version should be allowed unless there is a documented exception and approval path. If the content is sensitive or controlled, discovery of the alternate version should be further restricted so only authorized roles can see that it exists. The service should enforce both access control and status-based rules so the wrong version cannot be selected for formal use by accident. Only in rare cases where the authoritative version is unavailable, not yet published, or explicitly exempted for a specific mission need should a non-authoritative version be selectable for formal use, and that exception should require an approved waiver or designated authority sign-off. The system should record the justification, scope, and expiration of the exception, clearly flag the non-authoritative version in the UI and metadata, and automatically stop using it as the default once the authoritative version exists.
